chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Muhammad ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Marid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One should say during the Aqeeqa: 'O Allah, from You and for You is what You have gifted, and You gave it. O Allah, so accept from us upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and we seek refuge with Allah from the Pelted Satan.'
And you name [the animal], and slaughter it, and you say: 'For You I spill the blood, there is no associate for You, and the praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, expel the Pelted Satan.'

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ: The Pelted Satan, a common epithet for Satan in supplications
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqeeqa, the ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn child
key_terms.تَذْبَحُ: You slaughter, referring to the ritual act of sacrificing the animal
key_terms.رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: Lord of the worlds, a title for Allah
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ: The Sunnah of Your Prophet, referring to the prophetic tradition
key_terms.لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ: There is no associate for You, a declaration of monotheism (Tawhid)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers and phrases to recite during the Aqeeqa sacrifice in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the ritual etiquette for Aqeeqa, emphasizing the theological concept of divine ownership ('From You and to You') and the expulsion of Satan through specific invocations. It reflects the Shia tradition of combining gratitude for Allah's gift with the practical act of sacrifice, mirroring the Prophet's Sunnah to sanctify the child's entry into the world.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Muhammad Bin Hashim, from Muhammad Bin Marid, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘One should be saying during the Aqeeqa, ‘O Allahazwj! From Youazwj, and for Youazwj is what is Gifted, and Youazwj Gave it. O Allahazwj! So Accept from us upon the Sunnah of Yourazwj Prophetsaww, and we seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the Pelted Satanla’;

and you should name, and slaughter, and you should be saying, ‘For You<sup>azwj</sup> I spill the blood, there being no Associate for You<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds! O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Keep away the Pelted Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rashid from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Muhammad ibn Hashim from Muhammad ibn Marid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said to say this when offering ‘Aqiqah, ‘0 Lord, it is from You and for You is what You have granted. O Lord, accept it from us on the Sunnah of Your prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. We seek refuge with Allah against Satan, condemned to be stoned.’

Thereafter mention the name of the newborn , then slaughter the offering for ‘Aqiqah and say, Tor You I have spilled the blood and no one is Your partner. All praise belongs to Allah, Cherisher of the worlds. O Lord, drive away Satan, condemned to be stoned.’”
